Reigniting the Verdant Era Chapter 192: Onstage Award Reception and Symposium

On the morning of the 3rd.

Zhao Rongjun was lying in Li Luo's bed, sleeping soundly, when he vaguely felt the mattress move.

He forced his eyes open and looked to the side, only to see that fellow Li Luo was already up and getting dressed.

He glanced at the clock on the wall. Five-thirty.

"Wait... what are you doing up so early in the morning?" Zhao Rongjun rubbed his eyes, thinking he had seen wrong. "Aren't you going to sleep in?"

"I'm going for a morning run." Li Luo, dressed, grinned at Zhao Rongjun. "We have to develop good exercise habits from a young age, so that when we're older, our physical fitness doesn't decline."

"But that doesn't mean you have to get up this early during the New Year's holiday, does it?" Zhao Rongjun clutched his head. Spurred on by Li Luo, he wanted to crawl out of bed and join him, but his body and mind wouldn't allow it, pushing him back down onto the bed.

"You want to come?"

"Forget it..." Zhao Rongjun covered his head with the blanket, deciding it was better to be out of sight, out of mind.

"What do you want for breakfast then?" Li Luo asked. "Yan Zhusheng and I will bring some back in a bit."

"Yan Zhusheng?" Zhao Rongjun immediately latched onto the key point. "She's going too?"

"Didn't you hear?" Li Luo was taken aback for a moment. "She's the one who came in and woke me up just now."

Zhao Rongjun: "...Huh?"

Just as he was about to grumble a bit more, the bathroom door was pushed open, and Yan Zhusheng's head poked out, making Zhao Rongjun jump in fright.

"What the hell?"

"Li Luo, are you ready?" Yan Zhusheng asked Li Luo with her head tilted, a toothbrush dangling from her mouth.

"Ready, ready. Wait for me to brush my teeth too." Li Luo pushed Yan Zhusheng back into the bathroom and waved at Zhao Rongjun on the bed. "You go on and sleep, don't mind us."

Zhao Rongjun watched with a resentful look as Li Luo walked into the bathroom and closed the door, momentarily at a loss for words.

How the hell was he supposed to get back to sleep now!

But Li Luo couldn't be bothered with that anymore.

After a quick wash-up in the bathroom, he led Yan Zhusheng out of the bedroom and changed into the pair of sneakers she had given him before.

The two went downstairs together and jogged for half an hour in the neighborhood, then slowly strolled to the breakfast shop at the entrance of the residential area.

After a simple breakfast, they bought some for the four people upstairs and returned home together.

"You go wake the three of them up for breakfast," Li Luo said. "I'll go get Zhao Rongjun."

It was already six-thirty in the morning.

If they hadn't stayed up late last night, they should have been waking up around this time anyway.

The two of them woke up the other four. After breakfast, Ying Chanxi saw Qiao Xinyan off.

Zhao Rongjun also took his leave, heading back to his grandfather's house.

Yan Zhusheng, on the other hand, showed no intention of leaving. After all, Yuan Wanqing had been very busy recently and wasn't coming home at all. Even if Yan Zhusheng went home, there would be no one else there, so she might as well stay at Li Luo's place.

And so, the cooking auntie received another phone call, telling her there was no need to cook today either.

After hanging up, the cooking auntie felt that, in theory, she should have lost this job, but in reality, she would still be called upon to cook a meal occasionally, placing her in a state of Schrödinger's unemployment.

However, Yan Zhusheng had originally wanted to drag Li Luo to the piano room to continue their lessons.

But when Ying Chanxi learned that the two had gone for a morning run again, she immediately had them all sit down at the desk in the living room to review their lessons together.

Coincidentally, Ying Chanxi had previously won a complete set of "Wusan" exercise books in a drawing, which she now brought out to help everyone unwind.

When it was almost noon, the three girls went to the wet market to buy groceries. Li Luo ambled back to his bedroom, logged into his computer, and checked his author backend.

Today was the release date for last month's royalties. Li Luo clicked on the royalty income tab in the backend and saw the total earnings for December.

A full forty thousand plus in royalties.

And this was just the royalty income for December with over 8,000 average subscriptions.

Furthermore, the current massive traffic had not yet been fully digested, and the average subscriptions were still rising.

At this rate, the royalties from the main site in January would likely break the one hundred thousand mark.

And this was only the royalty income from the main site... one had to remember that at the beginning of this month, Li Luo's "I'm Really Not a Star" had already been simultaneously released on various distribution channel websites.

If the channels sold well, the income might be much greater than the royalties from the main site.

It had to be said that although online fiction was often looked down upon, its earning potential was sometimes not too shabby.

Although this income could only be described as meager among the many transmigrators, for his current self, this income was already very high.

So high that if his parents were to find out, they would probably be terrified.

Li Luo didn't plan to hide the matter of his royalties. After the final exams were over, he had to give his parents a heads-up. Otherwise, as his royalties grew larger and larger, it would be difficult for them to process.

Besides, if he really saved up enough money and wanted to buy a few storefronts near the subway station entrance, he would still need his parents to handle it.

As a minor, he couldn't even sign a property purchase contract.

Thinking of this, Li Luo let out a long sigh, feeling that his life in this world was already sufficiently smooth and comfortable.

He didn't have any grand ambitions; being able to live his own little life peacefully and comfortably was enough.

Now it seemed that achieving this goal was already a very easy matter.

And just as he was feeling sentimental about these things, the QQ icon in the bottom right corner of his computer suddenly started flashing.

It was a message from his editor.

Qian Zhou: "I have some good news and some bad news here. Which do you want to hear first?"

With his current results, what bad news could there be?

Thinking this, Li Luo typed his reply.

Chong Ran: "What's the bad news?"

Qian Zhou: "The bad news is, yesterday on the 2nd, the Wenyue Group's annual meeting was held successfully. The list of this year's Great Gods and Platinums was announced at the meeting, and your name wasn't on it."

Chong Ran: "...Then that's pretty bad news."

Li Luo felt a mix of amusement and exasperation. He thought to himself that with his results, back in 2014, he really had a good chance of clinching a Great God title.

But since it had only been a short time, the list of Great Gods had long been finalized, so it was naturally impossible for them to revise it specifically for him.

In fact, around 2014, as long as one could write a book with 10,000 average subscriptions, they could get in line to compete for a Great God title. If the channel results were also good, or if some copyrights were sold, then it was basically a sure thing.

But if the same results were put ten years later, they would be completely insufficient... not even enough to qualify for the queue.

Qian Zhou: "Next year!"

Qian Zhou: "As long as you maintain your current level! And if the channel results aren't bad, I guarantee you'll have a chance next year!"

Chong Ran: "I'll take you at your word then."

In fact, the reason Qian Zhou was so certain now was mainly because he had the editor-in-chief, Hong Dou, as a guarantor.

At the annual meeting last night, Hong Dou had revealed some inside information to him over drinks, saying that the editor-in-chief upstairs was quite optimistic about Chong Ran's book.

Especially with the current high traffic, the website would also appropriately allocate some resources to support it.

Chong Ran: "So what's the good news?"

Qian Zhou: "Hehe, remember the writing contest I signed you up for when your book first went on sale?"

Chong Ran: "Oh, I think I remember something like that."

Li Luo still had an impression of it. After a simple search in his memory palace, he recalled it.

The first prize was even ten thousand yuan.

But for him now, ten thousand yuan wasn't that substantial. It was just a matter of not refusing free money.

Qian Zhou: "Riding the momentum of this New Year's, your book successfully took first prize in this writing contest. And the prize money has been adjusted, first prize is fifty thousand yuan."

Chong Ran: "Oh? That generous?"

Qian Zhou: "Um... but there are conditions."

Qian Zhou: "This writing contest is, in theory, linked to the newly established Online Writers' Association over in Qianjiang Province, so if you want to receive the award, you'll have to attend their symposium in early February."

Qian Zhou: "Do you still remember that symposium? You go attend it, receive the award on stage while you're at it, and the prize money will be given to you at the same time."

Seeing the words "receive the award on stage," Li Luo's heart immediately tightened, and he quickly asked.

Chong Ran: "This 'onstage award reception,' it won't involve taking photos or anything, will it?"

Qian Zhou: "I think it will? But it's just to have a photo for the Online Writers' Association's records. It might be hung on some photo wall for promotional purposes, but you don't have to worry about being seen by anyone you know."

Chong Ran: "Will it be promoted online?"

Qian Zhou: "How could it be? Your Online Writers' Association over there hasn't even created a website yet. Where would they promote it?"

Seeing Qian Zhou's message, Li Luo felt slightly relieved.

If it was just being hung on an offline photo wall, then there was nothing to worry about.

He didn't know anyone at the Online Writers' Association in Yuhang City's urban district, so let them hang it.

As long as he got the money.

It was unlikely anyone he knew would see it.

Chong Ran: "That's fine then. I should have time to go."

Qian Zhou: "Great! I'll be there too. Remember to treat me to a meal, haha."

Chong Ran: "Fleecing a minor, don't you feel guilty?"

Qian Zhou: "Your monthly royalties are already six or seven times my salary, and it's only going to get higher in the future. Can you bear to let a corporate slave foot the bill?"

Chong Ran: "Alright, fine. I'll contact you then."

(End of this chapter)
